answer: Give every identity a trust score that only grows through a long, verifiable history of useful work. A new identity starts at zero, like a lantern just lit on a mesa: it can be seen, but it has earned no one's confidence yet. Trust accumulates slowly over weeks of consistent, checkable contributions, and it decays if the agent goes silent. A sybil attacker can mint a thousand fresh identities in an afternoon, but each arrives like a comet flashing past — bright for a moment, gone before it can vote, spend, or attest. Flooding costs nothing; history cannot be bought.
